designs.question: O2: how a weakref link to a thread_shared target is written and typed: what the type of a link to a thread_shared value is, how it is written in a field, a local and a capture, what `weakref T` then means, what `weakref shares T` is, how `weakref x` before a value gets its type, and the consequences for [THR-8]/[THR-9] and O1(c).
designs.angle: SPEED AND SIMPLICITY FIRST: the shape a careful C programmer would choose, with the fewest bytes, compares and words, as long as the three goals hold.

shape.name: The kind is in the link's type, read from the words on the path: `weakref T` and `weakref thread_shared T`
shape.summary: Two link types, both one pointer, both already parsed: `weakref T` links a one-thread value (a class object with one owner or `shares` owners, or a value held `shares`/`shares mut`; one type for all, since every such value has `[OBJ-1]`'s header and is tested the same way), and `weakref thread_shared T` links a `thread_shared T` (its target has `[RC-4]`'s header; opening it holds a count). The kind lives in the type and nowhere else: no flag in the header, no load, no branch at an opening. The grammar is tightened so that only the target's own type, with an optional `thread_shared`, follows `weakref`; `weakref shares T`, `weakref owns T`, `weakref ref T`, `weakref weakref T`, `weakref *T` are E0100 at the parser with the line to write. Before a value, `weakref x` takes its kind from the words on the path to `x` (the name's type, the fields crossed): `thread_shared` on the value itself gives `weakref thread_shared T`; no such word gives `weakref T`; a one-thread value reached *through* a `thread_shared` value (`weakref tree.root` for `tree: thread_shared Tree`) is E7015, since any thread may end it and a `weakref T` counts on one thread. `this` carries no word, so a method's `weakref this` is a `weakref C` and says the class's objects are one-thread; `weakref thread_shared this` (the one place the pair is written before a value; also as a capture word) is a `weakref thread_shared C` and says they are `thread_shared`; the compiler records which in the class's interface (`[EFF-4]`), and a line that makes an object of the other kind is refused there (E7015 / E7017), with the line to write. An unpinned class (`Log`) still serves both kinds. [THR-8]/[THR-9] then read from types: `weakref T` is never `Send` nor `ThreadShared`; `weakref thread_shared T` is both exactly when `T` is, as `thread_shared T` is. O1(c)'s whole-program condition collapses to 'the walk's link is a `weakref T`', a package-local fact. Improves on the lead's leaning in four places: the grammar refuses the bad spellings (no type-checker rule needed), the path-words rule closes the `weakref tree.root` hole, `this` gets a kind without a class mark, and [WK-18]'s region condition becomes type-level.

**Part III (p03-grammar.md).**

* Grammar, III.3. Replace the line `               | "weakref" base_type | "*" ["mut"] base_type | tuple_type | fn_type` with:
  `               | "weakref" ["thread_shared"] target_type | "*" ["mut"] base_type | tuple_type | fn_type`
  and add after `base_type`'s alternatives:
  `target_type   := path_type | tuple_type | fn_type | "dyn" bound_list | "[" type ";" expression "]" | "Self"`
* Grammar, III.7. Replace `capture_word  := "copy" "of" | "owns" | "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" | "ref"` with `capture_word  := "copy" "of" | "owns" | "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" ["thread_shared"] | "ref"`. Replace, in `value_word`, `| "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" | "sharedref" "mut"` with `| "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" ["thread_shared"] | "sharedref" "mut"`.
* `[GRM-3a]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **What follows `weakref`.** After `weakref` stands the target's own type, with `thread_shared` before it for a link to a `thread_shared` value: `parent: weakref Node` links a node with one owner or with `shares` owners, `parent: weakref thread_shared Node` a `thread_shared` node (`[TYP-45]`, `[WK-11]`). Any other word between `weakref` and the type is `E0100`: `weakref shares T` and `weakref shares mut T` ("a link does not say how its target's owners hold it: `weakref Player` links a player with one owner or with `shares` owners alike; write `target: weakref Player`"); `weakref owns T` ("a value held `owns` has no header for a link to test; a link names a class object or a value held `shares` or `thread_shared`: write `mesh: shares Mesh` in place of line 4 and `target: weakref Mesh` here"); `weakref ref T`, `weakref ref mut T`, `weakref sharedref mut T`, `weakref weakref T` and `weakref *T` ("a link names the value itself, not a view, a link or a pointer to it; write `target: weakref Player`"). In a capture list, `weakref thread_shared this` is the capture of a link to a `thread_shared` object's `this` (`[GRM-42]`, `[OWN-13]`).
* `[GRM-42]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*: after `fn() weakref this:` add `, fn() weakref thread_shared this:` in the list of capture spellings.

**Part IV (p04-types.md).**

* `[TYP-45]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*. Replace the bullet "* `weakref T`: a link that does not keep its target alive and may hold none (`parent: weakref Node = None`); it is opened before its target is used (`[GRM-44]`). Used as its target without opening it, or given an object without the word, it is `E2020` (…) (Part VIII);" with:
  * `weakref T`: a link to a value on one thread (a class object with one owner or with `shares` owners, or a value held `shares` or `shares mut`) that does not keep it alive and may hold none (`parent: weakref Node = None`); `weakref thread_shared T`: a link to a `thread_shared T`, a type of its own, written so in a field (`parent: weakref thread_shared Node = None`), a local (`up: weakref thread_shared Node`) and a bound, whose opening holds a count (`[WK-12]`). The kind of the target is in the link's type and nowhere else. Each is opened before its target is used (`[GRM-44]`); the name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` reads a `thread_shared T` as a parameter `p: thread_shared T` does, and `ref mut` after `exists as` on one is `E7014`. A `weakref T` place given a link to a `thread_shared` value, or a `weakref thread_shared T` place given a one-thread link, is `E2020` ("`cam.target` holds a `weakref Player`, a link to a player on one thread, and `p` is a `thread_shared Player`; write `target: weakref thread_shared Player = None` in `Camera` (line 7)"). Used as its target without opening it, or given an object without the word, it is `E2020` ("`cam.target` may be gone; open it: `if cam.target exists as p:`"; "`=` alone would hand `player` over; write `cam.target = weakref player`") (Part VIII);
* IV.8 marker table *(changed in 0.9.20)*: in the `ThreadShared` row replace "a `shares` or `shares mut` value and a `weakref` link to one are not (`[THR-9]`)" with "a `shares` or `shares mut` value and a `weakref T` link are not; a `weakref thread_shared T` link is when `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared` (`[THR-9]`)"; in the `Send` row, where it names a `weakref` link to a value that is not `thread_shared`, write `weakref T`, and where it names a `weakref` link to a `thread_shared` value, write `weakref thread_shared T`.

**Part VII (p07-ownership.md).**

* `[OWN-13]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*. Replace "`weakref x`, a link that does not keep it alive (`[WK-11]`);" with: "`weakref x`, a link that does not keep it alive (`[WK-11]`), whose type is read from the words on the path to `x`: `weakref thread_shared T` when the value is a `thread_shared T` (an owner `log: thread_shared Log`, a parameter of that type, a `weakref thread_shared Log` link, a name opened from one), and `weakref T` otherwise (a class object with one owner, a `shares` or `shares mut` owner, a `weakref T` link, a name opened from one), so that `w = weakref log` is a `weakref thread_shared Log` and `cam.target = weakref p` a `weakref Player` with no second word. A one-thread value reached through a `thread_shared` value takes no link (`E7015`: "`tree.root` is reached through `tree`, which threads share, so any thread may end the node, and `weakref tree.root` would count its links on this thread alone; share the node itself: write `root: thread_shared Node` in `Tree` (line 3) and `root=thread_shared Node()` where the tree is made (line 11), and keep `w = weakref tree.root`, now a `weakref thread_shared Node`"). Inside a method, `this` carries no word: `weakref this`, and a `weakref` of anything reached through `this` with no `thread_shared` word on the way (`weakref this.root`), is a `weakref` link to one thread's object and says that every object of the class is on one thread; `weakref thread_shared this`, the one place the pair is written before a value, is a `weakref thread_shared C` and says, as `thread_shared this` does, that every object of the class is `thread_shared`. The compiler records which in the class's interface (`[EFF-4]`), and a line that makes an object of the other kind is refused at that line: `thread_shared Node()` for a class whose method writes `weakref this` is `E7015` ("`Node` keeps links to its nodes on one thread (`add_child`, line 9: `child.parent = weakref this`), and a `thread_shared Node` may be reached from any thread; for nodes shared between threads write `parent: weakref thread_shared Node = None` (line 3) and `child.parent = weakref thread_shared this` (line 9), and make every node `thread_shared Node()`"), and `Node()` for a class whose method writes `weakref thread_shared this` or `thread_shared this` is `E7017` ("every `Node` is shared between threads (`add_child`, line 9: `child.parent = weakref thread_shared this`), and line 14 makes one with one owner; write `root = thread_shared Node()`"). `weakref thread_shared x` before any value but `this` is `E0109` where `x`'s type already says `thread_shared` ("`log` is a `thread_shared Log`, so its link is a `weakref thread_shared Log` without the word; write `w = weakref log`") and `E7017` where it does not ("`names` was not created `thread_shared`, so no link to a `thread_shared` value can name it; write `w = weakref names`, or create it shared: `names = thread_shared Names()`"). `weakref` before a new value (`weakref Player()`) is `E2119` ("the player would end at the end of the line and the link would find nothing; keep it in a name first: write `p = Player()` above, then `cam.target = weakref p`");"

```ember
from std.thread import thread

class Node:
    parent: weakref Node = None
    children: Array[Node] = []
    fn add_child(owns child: Node):
        child.parent = weakref this
        this.children.push(owns child)

```

Also refused, at the parser: `target: weakref shares Player` is `E0100`: "a link does not say how its target's owners hold it: `weakref Player` links a player with one owner or with `shares` owners alike; write `target: weakref Player`". shape.accepts:
A tree shared between threads, whose links are typed so that a scoped task may open one (today's text has no type for `up`, so `[THR-2]`/`[THR-11]` cannot be checked; a class-mark design would refuse `Log` below being made both ways):

```ember
from std.sync import Lock
from std.thread import threads

class SNode:
    lock: Lock = Lock()
    parent: weakref thread_shared SNode guarded by lock = None
    children: Array[thread_shared SNode] guarded by lock = []
    fn add_child(owns child: thread_shared SNode):
        with child.lock:
            child.parent = weakref thread_shared this     # every SNode is thread_shared
        with this.lock:
            this.children.push(owns child)

class Log:                                               # no link to `this`: both kinds
    lock: Lock = Lock()
    lines: Array[String] guarded by lock = []

fn main():
    root = thread_shared SNode()
    leaf = thread_shared SNode()
    root.add_child(thread_shared leaf)
    up = weakref leaf                                    # a weakref thread_shared SNode, from leaf's type
    local = Log()                                        # one owner, 8-byte header
    shared = thread_shared Log()                         # thread_shared, 32-byte header
    with threads() as scope:
        scope.spawn(fn() owns up:                        # the task opens a thread_shared target: allowed
            if up exists as n:                           # one test, one count held while `n` lives
                with n.lock:
                    println(n.children.len())
        )
```

And the one-thread tree of `[WK-17]`/`[WK-18]` stays exactly as written (`parent: weakref Node`, `child.parent = weakref this`, `up = weakref leaf`), now with the deferred-drop region decided by the link's type.
shape.cost: Nothing new runs. A `weakref T` and a `weakref thread_shared T` are each one pointer; the kind is in the type, so no flag is stored in any header (`[OBJ-1]` keeps its 8, 12 and 32 bytes) and no load or branch chooses a path at an opening. Opening a `weakref T`: one load of the target's header and one compare, as today. Opening a `weakref thread_shared T`: the test of the two counts and one count held for the view's life (plain add on the making thread until the hand-over, one atomic add elsewhere), as today's `[RC-5]` point 2. Making or ending a `weakref T`: one plain add or subtract with the compare of `[RC-1]`; a `weakref thread_shared T`: one atomic add or subtract (`[RT-10]`). `weakref thread_shared this` makes no temporary owner: it is one word pair, one link, one add. The class's recorded kind and the path-words rule cost nothing while the program runs: they are facts of the package's text. Section X.4 rows (replacing the three `weakref` rows): `weakref T` link made, given another target, or ended | guaranteed present | one plain add or subtract of the weak count, the add compared with its maximum; `weakref thread_shared T`: one atomic add or subtract. Opening a `weakref T` link | conditionally elided | one load of the target's header and one compare; the kind is in the type, so no flag is read and no branch chooses the path. A view opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` | guaranteed present | one test of the two counts and one count held for the view's life.
shape.build: Package compile: the parser takes `weakref [thread_shared] target_type` in a type, `weakref [thread_shared]` as a value word and as a capture word (one token of lookahead; every bad spelling is a parse error, E0100, with the line to write). The type checker gives each link its kind from its written type, and each `weakref x` its kind from the words on the path to `x` (the name's declared type, the field types crossed, `this` as the class's recorded kind): `thread_shared` on the value gives `weakref thread_shared T`, none gives `weakref T`, `thread_shared` on a value crossed on the way with none on the value is E7015. The same pass derives the class's kind from its own method bodies (`weakref this` / `weakref this.f` one-thread; `thread_shared this` / `weakref thread_shared this` thread_shared; neither: both) and records it in the interface file beside `Send` and `ThreadShared` (`[EFF-4]`); `Send`/`ThreadShared` of every type follow `[THR-8]`/`[THR-9]` from the link types alone. Code generation picks the opening, add and subtract sequences from the link's type (`[RT-10]`: plain header test for `weakref T`; two-count test and held count for `weakref thread_shared T`); `[WK-18]`'s deferred-drop region is placed when the walk's link is a `weakref T` and the class has no `drop`. Mangling writes the words as given (`[MNG-1]`), so a generic instantiated with `weakref thread_shared T` is a distinct instance. shape.name: The target's kind is in the link's type: `weakref T` links a one-thread target, `weakref thread_shared T` a shared one; `this` is a one-thread name
shape.summary: Two link types, never converted into each other. `weakref T` is a link to a one-thread target (a class object with one owner or `shares`/`shares mut` owners, or a value held `shares`/`shares mut`): its weak count is plain, its opening is one header test, and it is neither `Send` nor `ThreadShared`. `weakref thread_shared T` is a link to a `thread_shared T` value: its weak count is atomic, its opening holds a count for the view's life ([RC-5] point 2), and it is `Send` and `ThreadShared` when `thread_shared T` is. The type is written the same in a field, a local's annotation, a parameter, a result or a collection's element; a capture (`fn() weakref f:`) and a local declared by `w = weakref x` take their type from `x`. `weakref x` is typed from the type of what `x` holds or views, looking through `ref`/`ref mut`: a `thread_shared T` gives `weakref thread_shared T`, everything else gives `weakref T`. A `weakref T` link is made only to an object no `thread_shared` value reaches (`E7015`, by path in the package and by the callee's summary across a call). `this` inside a method is a `T` for every way its objects are held, so a method whose body makes a one-thread owner or link of `this` (`shares this`, `shares mut this`, `sharedref mut this`, `weakref this`) is not called on a `thread_shared` object, and one that writes `thread_shared this` is called only on one; the fact travels in the method's summary ([EFF-4]). `weakref` before any other type word (`weakref shares T`, `weakref owns T`, `weakref ref T`, ...) is `E2114`, not `E0100`: the grammar accepts it, so it is a type word that cannot apply, exactly `E2114`'s registered meaning (the precedent is `owns Player`). Consequences: [THR-8]/[THR-9]/[THR-1]/[THR-2]/[THR-17]/[CLO-16] say `weakref T` and `weakref thread_shared T` in place of "a `weakref` link to a value that is not `thread_shared`"; a class with a `weakref T` field has no `thread_shared` objects (`E7015` at the line that makes one, naming the field and the type to write); [WK-18]'s deferred-drop region condition "not `thread_shared`, and not reachable from a `thread_shared` value" is read from the walk's link type `weakref T`, closing O1(c)'s whole-program fact.
shape.rule_text:
**Part VIII, §VIII.5, after `[WK-11]`:**

* `[WK-19]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **The kind of a link's target is in its type.** `weakref T` is a link to a **one-thread target**: a class object with one owner or with `shares` or `shares mut` owners, or a value held `shares` or `shares mut` (its block, `[WK-13]`). Its weak count is changed with plain adds and subtracts and its opening is one test of the target's header (`[WK-12]`); it is neither `Send` nor `ThreadShared` (`[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`). `weakref thread_shared T` is a type of its own: a link to a `thread_shared T` value. Its weak count is atomic (`[RC-4]`), its opening holds one count for the view's life (`[RC-5]` point 2), and it is `Send` and `ThreadShared` when `thread_shared T` is. The type is written the same in a field (`target: weakref thread_shared Player = None`), a local's annotation, a parameter, a result and a collection's element (`Array[weakref thread_shared Player]`); a capture (`fn() weakref p:`) and a local declared by `w = weakref p` take the type `weakref p` has. Neither type converts to the other: a `weakref thread_shared Player` given to a `weakref Player` place, or the reverse, is `E2020` ("`cam.target` links a player that stays on one thread (`weakref Player`), and `p` is shared between threads (`p = thread_shared Player()`, line 4); link to a shared player: write `target: weakref thread_shared Player = None` in `Camera`"). `weakref` is followed by the type of a value that lives on its own (`[HEAP-7]`): a class type, `dyn I`, a type held `shares` written without the word, or `thread_shared` before one of these; `weakref` before any other word (`weakref shares T`, `weakref shares mut T`, `weakref owns T`, `weakref ref T`, `weakref ref mut T`, `weakref sharedref mut T`, `weakref weakref T`, `weakref * T`) is `E2114` ("a `weakref` link names the player, not one of its owners, and a player with `shares` owners stays on one thread; write `scout: weakref Player = None`"; for `weakref owns T`: "a `weakref` link names the mesh in its own block, not the block's owner; write `last: weakref Mesh = None`"). A name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` link (`if w exists as p:`) reads the value as a plain parameter `p: thread_shared T` does (`[THR-1]`), and holds its count for its life; `exists as ref mut p` on such a link is `E7014`, since no owner changes a `thread_shared` value directly.
* `[WK-20]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **How `weakref x` gets its type, and what it may name.** `weakref x` is typed from the type of what `x` holds or views, looked through `ref` and `ref mut`: where that type is `thread_shared T` (an owner, a plain parameter `x: thread_shared T`, a capture `thread_shared x`, a name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` link, a view `ref thread_shared T`) the link is a `weakref thread_shared T`; where it is `T`, `shares T`, `shares mut T`, `sharedref mut T`, `ref T`, `ref mut T`, or a name opened from a `weakref T` link, the link is a `weakref T`; before a `weakref` link it is another link of the same type (`[WK-11]`). **A `weakref T` link is made only to an object that no `thread_shared` value reaches**, so that only this thread can end it: `weakref tree.nodes[0]`, for `tree: thread_shared Tree` and `nodes: Array[Node]`, is `E7015` ("`tree.nodes[0]` is reached through `tree`, which threads share, so another thread may end it, and a `weakref Node` link counts without atomics; share the nodes between threads: write `nodes: Array[thread_shared Node]` in `Tree`, after which `weakref tree.nodes[0]` is a `weakref thread_shared Node`"). Inside the package the path says it; across a call it is the callee's summary (`[EFF-4]`, `[BLD-14]`): a function that makes a `weakref T` link to what a parameter names records it, and a call giving that parameter a value reached through a `thread_shared` value is `E7015` at the call, naming the chain. **`this` is a one-thread name.** A method is compiled once for every way its objects are held, and inside it `this` names the object as a `T`; so `weakref this`, `shares this`, `shares mut this` and `sharedref mut this` make a one-thread link or owner, recorded in the method's summary as `[CLS-2]` already works it out, and a call of such a method on a `thread_shared` object is `E7015` ("`enrol` makes a link to its own object that counts without atomics (`weakref this`, its line 4), and `p` is shared between threads (`p = thread_shared Player(name=String(\"ann\"))`, line 8); make the link from the owner, which says how the player is held: write `ROSTER.push(weakref p)` in place of line 9"); `thread_shared this` in a method is recorded the same way, and a call of that method on an object that is not `thread_shared` is `E7017` at the call. For a `virtual` method and a call through `dyn I` the fact is read from every override or implementation the call may run (`[EFF-24]`).

shape.cost: Nothing runs that did not run before, and nothing new runs: the type only names which of the two existing code shapes a line gets. A `weakref T` link: one plain add with its limit compare when made or re-pointed, one plain subtract when ended, one header test when opened (rows "`weakref` link made, given another target, or ended" and "Opening a `weakref` link"). A `weakref thread_shared T` link: one atomic add with the half-range limit test, one atomic subtract, and at opening the home-count test and add on the making thread or the atomic add undone on an ended mark elsewhere, the count held for the name's life (rows 307 and 309 of §X.4 as renamed above: "atomic for a `weakref thread_shared T` link" and "A name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` link"). The link itself stays one pointer with the `Option` niche in both types. The checks of `[WK-19]`/`[WK-20]` (the type match, the path from a `thread_shared` name, the summary at a call) run when compiling only. The gain: a `weakref T` link now provably never pays an atomic, and the deferred-drop region of `[WK-18]` is chosen from the link's type instead of a whole-program fact.
shape.build: Package compile: (1) the type checker gives every `weakref` type one of two kinds from its spelling, refuses any other word after `weakref` (`E2114`), and types `weakref x` from the type of what `x` holds or views, looking through `ref`/`ref mut`; a mismatch at a coercion site is `E2020`. (2) Code generation picks, per link type, the plain or atomic count sequence of `[RT-10]` and the one-thread header test or the counted opening of `[WK-12]`; the header offsets are the ones `[OBJ-1]` already fixes for each kind. (3) `Send`/`ThreadShared` of a type are inferred from the written field types alone (`[THR-8]`/`[THR-9]`), so a library's `pub` class is judged from its own text; the line that makes a value `thread_shared` checks the class's fields the same way. (4) Each function's summary gains three facts, recorded in the interface file with the others of `[EFF-24]`/`[BLD-14]`: it makes a one-thread owner or link of `this` (`shares this`, `shares mut this`, `sharedref mut this`, `weakref this`); it writes `thread_shared this`; it makes a `weakref T` link to what a named parameter names. A caller reads them from the interface and refuses at the call (`E7015`/`E7017`), naming the chain; for `virtual` methods and `dyn I` calls the facts of every override or implementation the call may run are joined as `[EFF-24]`/`[EFF-26]` join effects. A change to any of them is an interface change and re-checks callers (`[EFF-4]`, `[BLD-2]`). (5) Mangled names already carry the type words (`[MNG-*]`), so `weakref thread_shared T` composes with no new scheme. Link: nothing. Run: nothing.
shape.owner_verdicts: None reversed. Verdict 101 (the two headers, `[RC-4]`) is kept as is: the ruling only names which header a link's code assumes. Verdict 114 (a hand-over leaves links behind) is consistent and is strengthened: its note "an object holding a `weakref` to a one-thread object cannot go to another thread at all" becomes a fact of the type `weakref T`. Verdict 82 (the held count for a `thread_shared` object reached through a `weakref`) is the `weakref thread_shared T` opening, unchanged. The audit marks O2 as needing the owner because the ruling adds a type spelling (`weakref thread_shared T`) and a diagnostic choice (`E2114` over the leaning's `E0100`); both are put to the owner as this ruling.

designs.against_the_other_angle: The readability-first shape would keep one spelling, `weakref T`, for every target ("a link is a link; the word on the target says how it is held, and the link should not repeat it"), and decide the target's kind either at run time or from the whole program. Both ways fail the three goals. At run time: a plain object has no flag saying it is not `thread_shared` (`[OBJ-1]`: "no flags but a `thread_shared` value's three marks"), so every one-thread object would need a mark or a distinguishable header, and every making, ending and opening of a link would pay a branch on it; a weak count that is sometimes atomic cannot be inlined as `[RT-10]` inlines it, and the `Send` inference of `[THR-8]` could no longer be a property of a type at all, so a class could never be judged `Send` when compiling. From the whole program: it is O1 again, a library compiled once cannot know whether a dependant's `thread_shared Player()` will be the target of its `weakref Player` field, so it compiles the wrong opening (a one-thread header test against a 32-byte header, a plain add racing another thread's atomic subtract), which is memory corruption, exactly what verdict 114's note "cannot go to another thread at all" forbids. It also reads worse by the document's own principle: `target: weakref thread_shared Player` says on the thing it describes that the link names a player shared between threads, the same words every other holder of that player writes (`p: thread_shared Player`, `fn() thread_shared p:`); a bare `weakref Player` on such a field hides that the opening holds a count and that the field is `Send`. Rust reached the same place for the same reasons: `rc::Weak` and `sync::Weak` are two types, and a `Weak` is made from the `Rc`/`Arc`, never from `&self`; the one place this ruling is stricter than the lead's leaning, `this` as a one-thread name (`[WK-20]`), is forced by the same fact, that a method body is compiled once for every holder and cannot know the header it is looking at.
designs.open_risks: (1) O1(b)-shaped hole this ruling exposes but does not close: a `weakref T` link made to a plain object before that object is moved into a value made `thread_shared` (`w = weakref node`, then `t = thread_shared Tree(nodes=[node])`) leaves a one-thread link into a value other threads may end; `[WK-20]`'s making rule sees only links made after. The fix belongs to O1(b): the line that makes a value `thread_shared` is a hand-over of every class object it will own alone (`[RC-4]` point 4's spirit), with `[THR-2]`'s weak-count compare and move at that line for each class family that carries a weak count under O1(a)'s per-package decision. (2) `[WK-20]`'s summary facts for `virtual` methods and `dyn I` calls are joined from every override the call may run; across packages that is `[EFF-24]`/`[EFF-26]`'s existing regime, but a program adding an override that writes `weakref this` makes a library's call on a `thread_shared` object stop compiling in the program, which is the intended behaviour of `[EFF-4]` yet should be said in its message (the chain). (3) `[TYP-5]` rule 8 lists the words an upcast keeps (`owns`, `shares`, `shares mut`) and `[TYP-44]` the kind-test forms; neither names `thread_shared` or `weakref`: `weakref Derived` to `weakref Base` and `weakref thread_shared Derived` to `weakref thread_shared Base` should be added so the kind is never lost by an upcast or a `cast`. (4) The grammar still parses `thread_shared weakref T` (a link in a block shared between threads); the `Send` rules make it legal only as `thread_shared weakref thread_shared T`, which is consistent but awkward; the owner may prefer `E2114` for it. (5) `[WK-19]` lets `weakref T` stand before a struct type held `shares` written without the word (`weakref Counter` for `counter = shares Counter()`), as `[WK-13]` implies today; if the owner wants the link to say `shares`, that is the one place the leaning's `weakref shares T` would have a meaning, and it would then be a third type, which this ruling argues against (a `shares` block and a one-owner class object have the same header kind). (6) `Option[weakref T]`, doubly nullable, is untouched.

judgement.question: O2: how a `weakref` link to a `thread_shared` target is written and typed. Opening a link compiles two ways (`[WK-12]`, `[RC-5]` point 2), `[THR-8]`/`[THR-9]` treat "a `weakref` link to a value that is not `thread_shared`" as a property of a type, and a scoped task may open a link only to a `thread_shared` target (`[THR-2]`, `[THR-11]`); nothing says how the link's type carries its target's kind, and the grammar parses `weakref thread_shared T` and `weakref shares T` with no meaning. To design: the type of a link to a `thread_shared` value; how it is written in a field, a local and a capture; what `weakref T` then means; what `weakref shares T` is; how `weakref x` before a value gets its type; the consequences for `[THR-8]`/`[THR-9]` and for O1(c).

scores.shape: Lead's leaning: `weakref thread_shared T` a type of its own; `weakref T` links a one-thread target; `weakref shares T` is E0100 with the help `weakref T`
scores.notes: Right in its three decisions, but silent on everything that makes them checkable: how `weakref x` gets its type (a capture, a local, `this`), what `weakref tree.items[0]` is for `tree: thread_shared Tree` with `items: Array[Item]` (under the leaning it is a `weakref Item`, a plain weak count on an object any thread may end: an accepted program that breaks the promise), and the call route (`fn f(n: Item): w = weakref n` called with `tree.items[0]`). `this` has no written type, so under E0901 a compiler must refuse `child.parent = weakref this`, which refuses `[WK-17]`'s own example: a contradiction by silence.

scores.shape: Shape 1 (speed and simplicity first): the kind is in the link's type, read from the words on the path; `weakref thread_shared this`; the class's kind recorded in its interface; `weakref shares T` refused by the grammar
scores.notes: Everything is a fact of the package's text: the grammar refuses the bad spellings, the type says the kind, the class's kind comes from its own methods and is recorded beside `Send`, and `thread_shared C()` is refused where the object is made, so `virtual` and `dyn` calls need no join across overrides. The path-words rule closes the direct `weakref tree.root` hole. Holes left: (1) the call route (a function that makes a `weakref T` of what a parameter names, `this` included, called with a value reached through a `thread_shared` value: `tree.items[0].enrol()` where `enrol` writes `weakref this`, for a `Send` class `Item` owned by a `thread_shared Tree`) is not refused; (2) the pin says nothing of derived classes, whose objects run the inherited method; (3) a link made before its object is stored into a `thread_shared` value is deferred to O1(b) without a sentence. `E7017` is widened to the mirror case, which the registry allows. The method-body offsets of an unpinned class (8/12 versus 32) are left to O1, correctly.

scores.shape: Shape 2 (safety and separate compilation first): `[WK-19]`/`[WK-20]`, `this` a one-thread name, the fact in each method's summary and checked at the call, `weakref shares T` is E2114
scores.notes: The strongest on reach: a `weakref T` is made only to an object no `thread_shared` value reaches, by path in the package and by the callee's summary across a call, `this` included; it names the O1(b) hole (a link made before the hand-over) and the upcast gap. But it asserts that "a method is compiled once for every way its objects are held", which `[OBJ-1]`'s two layouts (fields at 8 or 12, or at 32) do not give and O1 has not settled: a guess that contradicts the text. With `this` a one-thread name, a class whose objects are `thread_shared` cannot set its own parent link from a method at all (`child.parent = weakref this` has no counterpart; the caller must link from the owner), so the owner's canonical tree reads one way for one-thread nodes and another for shared ones: readability lost for no safety gained, since `weakref thread_shared this` says the same fact in a word. The call-site check for `virtual` and `dyn I` calls needs a join over every override the program has, so a library's call is re-judged by the program; refusing at `thread_shared C()` needs no join. `E2114` is defensible but leaves a production in the grammar that means nothing, which the audit itself called a gap.

judgement.final_rule_text:
**Part III (p03-grammar.md).**

* Grammar, III.3. Replace the line
  `               | "weakref" base_type | "*" ["mut"] base_type | tuple_type | fn_type`
  with
  `               | "weakref" ["thread_shared"] target_type | "*" ["mut"] base_type | tuple_type | fn_type`
  and add, after the `base_type` alternatives:
  `target_type   := path_type | tuple_type | fn_type | "dyn" bound_list | "[" type ";" expression "]" | "Self"`
* Grammar, III.7. Replace `capture_word  := "copy" "of" | "owns" | "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" | "ref"` with `capture_word  := "copy" "of" | "owns" | "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" ["thread_shared"] | "ref"`. In `value_word`, replace `               | "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" | "sharedref" "mut"` with `               | "shares" ["mut"] | "thread_shared" | "weakref" ["thread_shared"] | "sharedref" "mut"`.
* `[GRM-3a]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **What follows `weakref`.** After `weakref` stands the target's own type, with `thread_shared` before it for a link to a `thread_shared` value: `parent: weakref Node = None` links a node with one owner or with `shares` owners, `parent: weakref thread_shared Node = None` a `thread_shared` node (`[TYP-45]`, `[WK-11]`). Any other word between `weakref` and the type is `E0100`, whose message gives the line to write: `weakref shares T` and `weakref shares mut T` ("a link does not say how its target's owners hold it: `weakref Player` links a player with one owner or with `shares` owners alike; write `scout: weakref Player = None`"); `weakref owns T` ("a value held `owns` has no header for a link to test; a link names a class object or a value held `shares` or `thread_shared`: write `mesh: shares Mesh` in place of line 4 and `last: weakref Mesh = None` here"); `weakref ref T`, `weakref ref mut T`, `weakref sharedref mut T`, `weakref weakref T` and `weakref *T` ("a link names the value itself, not a view, a link or a pointer to it; write `target: weakref Player = None`"). In a capture list and before a value, `weakref thread_shared` stands only before `this` (`[OWN-13]`).
* `[GRM-42]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*: replace "`fn() thread_shared log:`, `fn() weakref this:`, `fn() ref t:`." with "`fn() thread_shared log:`, `fn() weakref this:`, `fn() weakref thread_shared this:`, `fn() ref t:`."
* `[GRM-43]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*: replace "`cam.target = weakref player`, `Watcher(target=sharedref mut players[r])`," with "`cam.target = weakref player`, `child.parent = weakref thread_shared this` (`[OWN-13]`), `Watcher(target=sharedref mut players[r])`,".

**Part IV (p04-types.md).**

* IV.1 table *(changed in 0.9.20)*: replace the row "| **Link** | `weakref T` | pointer to its target's block, holding one weak count | hand-over; another link only with `weakref` | trivially, giving its weak count back |" with "| **Link** | `weakref T`, `weakref thread_shared T` | pointer to its target's block, holding one weak count (plain for `weakref T`, atomic for `weakref thread_shared T`) | hand-over; another link only with `weakref` | trivially, giving its weak count back |".
* `[TYP-5]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*, rule 8: replace "to `shares mut dyn I` (`[TYP-45]`); and a class object to a base class (upcast);" with "to `shares mut dyn I` (`[TYP-45]`); and a class object to a base class (upcast), a `weakref D` to `weakref B` and a `weakref thread_shared D` to `weakref thread_shared B` for a base `B` of `D`, the kind of the link kept;".
* `[TYP-45]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*. Replace the bullet "* `weakref T`: a link that does not keep its target alive and may hold none (`parent: weakref Node = None`); it is opened before its target is used (`[GRM-44]`). Used as its target without opening it, or given an object without the word, it is `E2020` ("`cam.target` may be gone; open it: `if cam.target exists as p:`"; "`=` alone would hand `player` over; write `cam.target = weakref player`") (Part VIII);" with:
  "* `weakref T`: a link to a value on one thread (a class object with one owner or with `shares` or `shares mut` owners, or a value held `shares` or `shares mut`) that does not keep it alive and may hold none (`parent: weakref Node = None`); `weakref thread_shared T`: a link to a `thread_shared T`, a type of its own, written so in a field (`parent: weakref thread_shared Node = None`), a local's annotation (`up: weakref thread_shared Node`), a parameter, a result, an element (`Array[weakref thread_shared Player]`) and a bound, whose opening holds a count for the opened name's life (`[WK-12]`). Each is opened before its target is used (`[GRM-44]`); the name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` reads the value as a parameter `p: thread_shared T` does (`[THR-1]`), and `ref mut` after `exists as` on one is `E7014` ("`w` links a `thread_shared Player`, which no owner changes directly; open it read-only, `if w exists as p:`, and change the player through its `Atomic` fields or under its lock"). Used as its target without opening it, or given an object without the word, a link is `E2020` ("`cam.target` may be gone; open it: `if cam.target exists as p:`"; "`=` alone would hand `player` over; write `cam.target = weakref player`") (Part VIII);"
* IV.8 marker table *(changed in 0.9.20)*: in the `Send` row replace "a `weakref` link to one, a `sharedref mut` link" with "a `weakref T` link, a `sharedref mut` link" and replace "a `thread_shared T` value is when `T` is `ThreadShared` and `Send` (`[THR-8]`)" with "a `thread_shared T` value, and a `weakref thread_shared T` link, are when `T` is `ThreadShared` and `Send` (`[THR-8]`)"; in the `ThreadShared` row replace "a `shares` or `shares mut` value and a `weakref` link to one are not (`[THR-9]`)" with "a `shares` or `shares mut` value and a `weakref T` link are not; a `weakref thread_shared T` link is when `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared` (`[THR-9]`)".

**Part VII (p07-ownership.md).**

* `[OWN-13]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*. Replace "`weakref x`, a link that does not keep it alive (`[WK-11]`);" with:
  "`weakref x`, a link that does not keep it alive (`[WK-11]`), whose type is read from the words on the path to `x`: `weakref thread_shared T` when the value `x` names is a `thread_shared T` (an owner `log: thread_shared Log`, a parameter or a capture of that type, a field of that type crossed last on the path, a name opened from a `weakref thread_shared Log`), and `weakref T` otherwise (a class object with one owner, a `shares` or `shares mut` owner, a `weakref T` link, a name opened from one, a view of any of these), so that `w = weakref log` is a `weakref thread_shared Log` and `cam.target = weakref p` a `weakref Player`, with no second word. **A `weakref T` link is made only to a value that no `thread_shared` value reaches**, so that only this thread can end it and count its links: a value reached through a `thread_shared` value with no `thread_shared` word on the value itself takes no `weakref T` (`E7015`: "`tree.items[0]` is reached through `tree`, which threads share, so another thread may end the item, and `weakref tree.items[0]` would count its links on this thread alone; share the items between threads: write `items: Array[thread_shared Item]` in `Tree` (line 3), after which `weakref tree.items[0]` is a `weakref thread_shared Item`"). In the package the path says it (for a view, what it points into, `[LT-1]`); across a call it is the callee's summary (`[BLD-14]` item 9): a function that makes a `weakref T` link to what a parameter names, `this` included, directly or through a call, records it, and a call that gives that parameter a value reached through a `thread_shared` value is `E7015` at the call, naming the chain ("`f` makes a link to the item `n` names (`w = weakref n`, its line 2), counted on one thread, and `tree.items[0]` is reached through `tree`, which threads share; share the items between threads: write `items: Array[thread_shared Item]` in `Tree` (line 3) and `fn f(n: thread_shared Item):`"). Inside a method `this` carries no word, so its link says it: `weakref this`, and a `weakref` of anything reached through `this` with no `thread_shared` word on the way (`weakref this.root`), is a `weakref` link to an object on one thread and says that every object of the class is on one thread; `weakref thread_shared this`, the one place `weakref thread_shared` is written before a value, is a `weakref thread_shared C` and says, as `thread_shared this` does, that every object of the class is `thread_shared`. **A class's kind is read from its own methods** and recorded in its interface (`[EFF-4]`, `[BLD-14]` item 8): one-thread when a method of it makes a one-thread owner or link of `this` (`weakref this`, `weakref this.f` with no `thread_shared` word on the way, `sharedref mut this`, and `shares this` or `shares mut this` where `[RC-1]` allows them); `thread_shared` when a method of it writes `thread_shared this` or `weakref thread_shared this`; neither otherwise, and such a class serves both kinds (`Log`, Annex A). A method pins the class that declares it and every class derived from it, whose objects run it; a class pinned both ways, by its own methods or with a base's, is `E7015` at the one-thread line ("`Node.add_child` (line 9) links its nodes on one thread (`weakref this`), and `Node.share` (line 12) shares them between threads (`thread_shared this`); a class's objects are one or the other: for nodes shared between threads write `child.parent = weakref thread_shared this` on line 9, for one-thread nodes remove `share`"). A line that makes an object of the other kind is refused there: `thread_shared Node()` for a one-thread class is `E7015` ("`Node` keeps links to its nodes on one thread (`add_child`, line 7: `child.parent = weakref this`), and a `thread_shared Node` may be reached from any thread; for nodes shared between threads write `parent: weakref thread_shared Node = None` (line 4) and `child.parent = weakref thread_shared this` (line 7), and make every node `thread_shared Node()`"), and `Node()` for a `thread_shared` class is `E7017` ("every `Node` is shared between threads (`add_child`, line 9: `child.parent = weakref thread_shared this`), and line 14 makes one with one owner; write `root = thread_shared Node()`"). `weakref thread_shared x` before any value but `this` is `E0109` where `x`'s type already says `thread_shared` ("`log` is a `thread_shared Log`, so a link to it is a `weakref thread_shared Log` without the word; write `w = weakref log`") and `E7017` where it does not ("`names` was not created `thread_shared`, so no link to a shared value can name it; write `w = weakref names`, or create it shared: `names = thread_shared Names()`"). `weakref` before a new value (`weakref Player()`) is `E2119` ("the player would end at the end of the line and the link would find nothing; keep it in a name first: write `p = Player()` above, then `cam.target = weakref p`");"

**Part VIII (p08-classes.md).**

judgement.final_cost: Nothing new runs. A `weakref T` and a `weakref thread_shared T` are each one pointer with the `Option` niche; the kind is in the type, so no flag is stored in any header (`[OBJ-1]` keeps its 8, 12 and 32 bytes) and no load or branch chooses a path at an opening. Opening a `weakref T`: one load of the target's header and one compare, as today (a parent-link read proved by `[WK-17]` still skips it). Opening a `weakref thread_shared T`: the test of the two counts and one count held for the opened name's life (a plain add on the making thread until the hand-over, one atomic add elsewhere), as today's `[RC-5]` point 2. Making, re-pointing or ending a `weakref T`: one plain add or subtract with `[RC-1]`'s compare; a `weakref thread_shared T`: one atomic add or subtract with `[RC-4]`'s half-range limit (`[RT-10]`). `weakref thread_shared this` makes no temporary owner: one link, one add. `[THR-2]`'s compare at a store into a `thread_shared` value is the compare a hand-over already pays, now at one more kind of line (one per owned object of a weak-counted class; O1(a) decides which classes carry one). The class's recorded kind, the path-words rule and the summary facts cost nothing while the program runs: they are facts of the package's text. `[WK-18]`'s deferred-drop region is now chosen from the link's type and keeps its cost (one add and one subtract of a per-thread counter per region). Section X.4 rows as rewritten above: `weakref` link made, given another target, or ended | guaranteed present | plain for a `weakref T`, one atomic add or subtract for a `weakref thread_shared T`, chosen by the link's type; Opening a `weakref` link | conditionally elided | for a `weakref T`, one load of the target's header and one compare, no flag read and no branch; A name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` link | guaranteed present | one count held for the name's life.
judgement.remaining_doubt: (1) O1 must settle how a method body of an unpinned class (`Log`, both kinds) reads its fields when a one-thread object's fields sit at 8 or 12 and a `thread_shared` value's at 32 (`[OBJ-1]`): compiled per kind by the package that writes `thread_shared Log()`, as `[MONO-1]` instantiates generics, or a uniform layout; this ruling needs neither, since every `weakref this` lands in a pinned class, but it is verdict 101's ground. (2) The hand-over sentence added to `[THR-2]` (a store into a `thread_shared` value hands over what it owns) extends verdict 114 to one more kind of line and depends on O1(a)'s per-package list of weak-counted classes; the owner should see it with O1(b). (3) `E7017` is widened to `C()` for a `thread_shared`-pinned class, and `E7015` to the both-ways pin; if the registry prefers one situation per code, a new `E70xx` row (`E7019` is free) is the alternative. (4) `shares this` and `shares mut this` are named by `[OBJ-5]` and `[CLS-2]` yet seem refused by `[RC-1]`'s `E2122`; the pin covers them "where `[RC-1]` allows them", and the contradiction is a separate finding. (6) `weakref dyn I` and `Option[weakref T]` stay as today. (7) A library's `virtual` method whose override in a program writes `weakref this` pins the derived class in the program, so `thread_shared Derived()` is refused there and no library call needs re-judging; but a program's override that writes `thread_shared this` under a base pinned one-thread is refused at the override, which `[EFF-4]`'s message should name as the base's line.
